research.role: STEP Intern (Student Training in Engineering Program)
research.job_description_summary: Google hires students and early-career engineers in India through programmes such as STEP (internship) and early-career Software Engineer roles. Glassdoor STEP Intern reviews (July and October 2026) describe a 15-minute recruiter call, three 45-minute technical coding rounds (sliding window, hashing, trees such as a modified lowest common ancestor) and team matching. The official careers pages were not fetched.
required_skills: Coding in a language of choice
limitations: Google's official careers pages were not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.

STEP rounds are REPORTED from a handful of Glassdoor reviews that mostly give no problem text; only two details are specific (sliding window with follow-ups, and a modified LeetCode lowest common ancestor). Those items are class B, one report each, unverified.

The Software Engineer, Early Career track has no India-specific candidate reports found; its rounds are marked PROPOSED (an online assessment, two coding interviews and a Googleyness round) and all of its questions are original practice.
Google does not publish its question bank; STEP is an internship programme, so STEP content is for intern-to-new-grad preparation.
Behavioral prompts follow Google's publicly described 'Googleyness' themes and are original.
One 2026 Glassdoor review (accepted offer) says only that the problems were LeetCode-style.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.
